dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: āsane śayane sthitvā nirādhāraṃ vibhāvayan | svadehaṃ manasi kṣīṇe kṣaṇāt kṣīṇāśayo bhavet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
sanskrit_variants: verse 82: GRETIL (and Pradīpaka) read kṣiṇe; corrected to kṣīṇe with Wallis (the same line has kṣīṇāśayo).
dharana.rendering: Resting on a seat or a bed, let one contemplate one's own body as without support; as the mind fades, in an instant one becomes free of one's stored dispositions.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: though actually resting on a seat or bed, one contemplates with firm conviction that the body has no support at all; the mind becomes free of the thought-constructs that serve as its props, and with that the habitual tendencies (vāsanā) lying in the unconscious also vanish. Wallis: 'floating without support'.
dharana.instruction: Resting on a seat or bed, feel your body as if nothing were holding it up.

The Mystery Within (2019), parallel translations: 'Dharana 59 • verso 82' (agrees)

verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Sitting on a seat or lying on a bed, as the verse says; fully supported in fact.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 82 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is the body pictured floating, with nothing beneath it, while in fact it rests on a seat or bed.
geometry.svg_hint: a body outline with a clear gap beneath it, floating in open space
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Float free
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the felt need for support falls away, and old mental grooves loosen with it. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Feel the body as if nothing were holding it up
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The body felt as unsupported, floating
attention.secondary: The mind growing quiet as it loses its props

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Resting on a seat or a bed, let one contemplate one's own body as without support; as the mind fades, in an instant one becomes free of one's stored dispositions.
adiyogi.method_summary: Sit on a seat or lie on a bed, fully supported. Then contemplate the body as having no support at all, as if floating in open space. Let the mind quieten as it loses its props.

honesty.disclosure: Door 059 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 59 (verse 82) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 059 is dharana 59, verse 82. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. If the floating image brings unease or a falling feeling, feel the support again and open the eyes. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
